narrative: The model estimated a 64.9% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a risk estimate, not a certainty, but it was high enough that your law school application was rejected. In the model’s ranking, your third-year class standing was the strongest factor: at decile 1.00, compared with an average of about 5.79 among accepted students, it pushed the prediction toward failure. Your family income bracket was the second most influential factor; being in the middle-income group modestly pushed toward passing, so it worked in your favor rather than against you. Your LSAT score was the third most influential factor: 22.70 versus an accepted-student average of 37.18 pushed the prediction toward failure. The model did not use your gender or race. To improve a future application, focus on what you can change: raise your academic standing, prepare thoroughly for a higher LSAT score, and consider delaying application until you have stronger evidence of bar-exam readiness. You may also ask admissions for feedback and address any personal circumstances that affected your grades.
